theme: 3 terms on moving between screens: the container with a stack of screens, sliding a new screen onto that stack, and showing a screen on top for a separate task

terms.definition: A container that manages a stack of screens and shows a bar with a back button.
terms.example: Wrap the list in a Navigation Controller, then the title bar comes for free.

terms.definition: Moving to a new screen that slides in from the side and is added to the stack, with a back button.
terms.example: Use Push Navigation for the detail screen, users expect a back button there.

terms.definition: Showing a screen on top of the current one, usually sliding up, for a separate task.
terms.example: Settings opens as a Modal Presentation, with a Done button at the top.

quizzes.question: In this code, how is `editor` shown?
quizzes.code:
let editor = EditorVC()
present(editor, animated: true)

video.title: Navigation Controller, Push Navigation & Modal Presentation | Day 89
video.description:
Learn to explain how iOS apps move between screens: Navigation Controller, Push Navigation & Modal Presentation, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
Navigation Controller - A container that manages a stack of screens and shows a bar with a back button.
Push Navigation - Moving to a new screen that slides in from the side and is added to the stack, with a back button.
Modal Presentation - Showing a screen on top of the current one, usually sliding up, for a separate task.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

Day 89 of the iOS Daily English series: 3 terms a day, from Swift basics to advanced iOS.

#Shorts #iOSDev #Swift #LearnEnglish

landscape.description:
Explain Navigation Controller, Push Navigation & Modal Presentation in UIKit by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
내비게이션 컨트롤러, 푸시 내비게이션, 모달 프레젠테이션 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

Navigation Controller - A container that manages a stack of screens and shows a bar with a back button.
한국어: 내비게이션 컨트롤러: 화면 스택을 관리하고 뒤로 가기 버튼이 있는 바를 보여주는 컨테이너

Push Navigation - Moving to a new screen that slides in from the side and is added to the stack, with a back button.
한국어: 푸시 내비게이션: 새 화면이 옆에서 밀려 들어와 스택에 쌓이고 뒤로 가기 버튼이 생기는 화면 이동

Modal Presentation - Showing a screen on top of the current one, usually sliding up, for a separate task.
한국어: 모달 프레젠테이션: 별도의 작업을 위해 현재 화면 위에, 보통 아래에서 올라오며 화면을 띄우는 것

In this video, Mina and Jake find out why a detail screen has no back button and a push inside a modal does nothing, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: The detail screen has no back button. Can you explain why in English?

dialogue.title: Where is the back button?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, the detail screen opens, but there's no back button.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You `present` it, so that's a Modal Presentation. It slides up from the bottom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shouldn't detail screens slide in from the side?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. Use Push Navigation, and the back button comes for free.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right, on the Navigation Controller that holds this list screen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And the compose screen, push or modal?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Modal Presentation fits there. It's a separate task the user finishes or cancels.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But inside compose I push a picker, and nothing happens.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The modal has no Navigation Controller, so Push Navigation silently does nothing. Wrap it in one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Got it. Push to drill down, modal for separate tasks.
No back button? The screen needs a Navigation Controller.
